close_reason:
chat_create refactored to match-as-expression: 'let (create_obj, client_id_opt) = match input { ... }'. Each arm now evaluates to a (Value, Option<&str>) tuple instead of using deferred-init bindings outside the match.

Group arm retains its early-return on empty name — 'return Err(...)' is allowed inside match arms.

Behaviour-equivalent. cargo test -p jmap-chat-client green, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean.

space.rs:180-186 referenced in the bead is a single-branch conditional-build (no match), already idiomatic. message.rs is single-branch and irrelevant per the bead's own note.

Committed as 10c84b2.
description: chat.rs:185-249 declares 'let create_obj;' outside the match and assigns inside each arm. The idiomatic Rust pattern is match-as-expression: 'let (create_obj, client_id_opt) = match input { Direct {...} => (json!(...), *client_id), Group {...} => (...), Channel {...} => (...) };'. The deferred-init form works but is ML-style rather than Rust-style — readers expect match-to-be-an-expression and have to do extra work to parse the deferred-init pattern. Engineering basis: maintainability — match-as-expression is the established Rust idiom for this exact shape (build different values per variant). Same pattern appears in space.rs:180-186 (smaller, less impactful) and message.rs:172-181 (single-branch, irrelevant).
title: ChatCreateInput create_obj uses deferred-init binding instead of match-as-expression
